stem.en: When is the average speed of an object equal to the magnitude of its average velocity?

text.en: When it returns to its starting point

feedback.en: Then the average velocity is zero but the average speed is not.

text.en: When it moves in one direction without turning back

feedback.en: Right. Then the distance travelled equals the magnitude of the displacement.
Not when it turns back. Then the displacement is smaller than the distance.

explanation.en: Average speed uses the distance travelled; average velocity uses the displacement. They have the same size only when the distance equals the magnitude of the displacement, that is, when the object never turns back.

hints.en: When is the distance travelled equal to the magnitude of the displacement?
